question.text: Conquistadors from this European nation conquered the Incas. This empire established colonies in all of Central America and most of South America.
question.clue: A city controlled by this country was twice attacked by the pirate Limahong.

swap.leadin: In North America, this conflict was known as Queen Anne's War.
swap.text: Name this war which was fought to prevent the uniting of the French and Spanish crowns.
swap.clue: The North American theater of this conflict was known as Queen Anne's War.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Portuguese colonial history.
question.text: Later modified by the Treaty of Zaragoza to include the Moluccas, this treaty set up a line of demarcation dividing the world between Spain and Portugal.
question.clue: This treaty established a line 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands, which was later extended through both poles by the Treaty of Zaragoza.

swap.text: The expeditions of Columbus were sponsored by this queen, who ruled Spain on equal terms alongside her husband Ferdinand.
swap.answerHtml: Queen Isabella [or Isabella I; or Isabella the Catholic; accept, but DO NOT REVEAL, Isabella of Castile]

question.text: This party was the only legal party in Spain during Franco's rule. This fascist political party merged with the Carlists and was dissolved in 1977.
question.answerHtml: Falange (or Traditionalist Spanish Phalanx of the Committees of the National Syndicalist Offensive or that in Spanish)
question.clue: Two leaders of this party were buried within the Santa Cruz Basilica at the Valley of the Fallen.

swap.leadin: The Iberian Peninsula was subject to this war movement in resistance to Muslim rule.
swap.text: This period of Iberian history consists of Christians retaking Spain from the Moors.
swap.clue: The eventual victors in this conflict collected a tribute called the paria from the ta'ifa principalities that emerged after the collapse of the Almohad Caliphate.

question.leadin: Prior to the defeat of this force, one monarch claimed that she had "the heart and stomach of a king."
question.text: Name this invading military force which was hindered by the "Protestant wind" and defeated at the Battle of Gravelines ["gravf-leen"].
question.answerHtml: The Spanish Armada (or Grande y Felicísima Armada; prompt on “Spanish navy” and equivalents)
question.clue: The plan was for this force to join with one under Alessandro Farnese, but before that could happen, it participated in its first engagement off Eddystone.

swap.text: The Sicilian Vespers happened concurrently with a crusade named after this region. A ruler of this Spanish region issued the Alhambra Decree and married Germaine de Foix.
swap.clue: This polity conquered Sicily in the wake of the Sicilian Vespers Uprising in 1282 during the reign of its "Great" king, Peter III.

question.text: The Second Macedonian War was prompted by this king's adventures in the Mediterranean, including a defeat at the hands of Rhodes near Chios in 201 BCE. His son Demetrius was restored to him in 190 after keeping the peace with Rome for seven years.
question.clue: This king's opponents claimed that his reign was a violation of the Hague Partition Treaties.

swap.leadin: Although over 33,000 people are buried in this location, only two of the graves have names attached to them.
swap.text: Name this memorial erected with coerced labor in the Sierra de Guadarrama foothills. A massive stone cross stands out from this burial site of Jose Antonio Primo de Rivera.
swap.answerHtml: Valley of the Fallen [or Valle de los Caídos]
swap.clue: In 2019, Franco's body was exhumed from this location in Spain, which includes the tallest memorial cross in the world and the remains of people who fought on both sides of the Civil War

question.text: This grandson of Alfonso XIII officially ended the Spanish monarchy's right to name Roman Catholic bishops in 1976. He also teased the conservative King of Belgium while signing off on legalizing gay marriage in Spain in 2005.
question.answerHtml: King Juan Carlos I [or Juan Carlos Alfonso Víctor María de Borbón y Borbón-Dos Sicilias]
question.clue: A June 2014 decision by this man led to a rise in rank for former television anchor Letizia Ortiz.

swap.leadin: This man presided over the economic growth called the "Spanish Miracle."
swap.text: Name this dictator of Spain who took power in the Spanish Civil War. He restored the monarchy by naming Prince Juan Carlos as the King of Spain and his successor.
swap.clue: He responded to the communist-backed "Red Terror" by initiating the "White Terror," which lasted into his reign.

question.text: The 1874 Bourbon Restoration placed the twelfth king of this name on the Spanish throne. The tenth king of this name ruled Castile in the 13th century and is known as "the Wise."
question.answerHtml: Alfonso [accept Alfonso XII; accept Alfonso X or Alfonso the Wise]
question.clue: The first aforementioned ruler of this name ordered the compilation of the legal code Siete Partidas and was known as the Wise.

swap.text: In modern times, this Spanish General put down a Syndicalist revolt in Asturias in the lead up to the Spanish Civil War. This dictator defeated the Republican forces of Manuel Azana in that civil war and ruled Spain for forty years.
swap.clue: This leader created an air bridge using Junker-52s to deploy his Army of Africa in a coup against Manuel Azana's Popular Front.

question.leadin: The Duke of Wellington created the lines of Torres Vedras to protect one capital in this conflict, which was triggered by an 1807 invasion led by Jean-Andoche Junot.
question.text: Name this conflict in which Napoleon's forces invaded Spain and Portugal.
question.clue: During this war, defeats at Vitoria and Salamanca undermined the rule of Joseph Bonaparte, who fought against an allied force led by the Duke of Wellington.

swap.leadin: This man was exiled after the unauthorized Battle of Cabra, which angered Alfonso VI.
swap.text: Name this man who spent around six years serving the Moorish leader of Zaragoza, during which he frequently fought such Christian kingdoms as Aragon and also earned a nickname that probably means "The Lord."
swap.answerHtml: El Cid (el seed or el theeth) [or Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar; accept El Campeador]
swap.clue: This ruler of Valencia who fought both for and against the Taifa of Zargoza.

question.leadin: Abd-ar-Rahman I erected the Great Mosque of this city above the church of Saint Vincent, beginning the Emirate which lasted from 750 to 929 CE.
question.text: Name this city which remained the de facto capital of al-Andalus for almost 300 years. After rule by Hisham II and his chancellor Almanzor until 1031 CE, this city's Caliphate broke up into taifa kingdoms.
question.clue: Mozarabs like Paul Alvar and Eulogius were hanged in this city during its namesake "Martyrs Movement."

swap.text: Throughout the fifteenth century, Naples was in a personal union with this Spanish kingdom, which gained control of Sicily at the end of the Sicilian Vespers.
swap.clue: Pope Martin IV ("the fourth") ordered a crusade against this kingdom after its ruler Peter III ("the third") accepted a request to invade Sicily in response to the Sicilian Vespers.

question.leadin: This concept is defined as "life, borne by living societies founded in its name" in French historian Pierre Nora's work on its "sites," or lieux.
question.text: Identify this concept that names a 2007 law that banned Francoists from rallying at the Valley of the Fallen, in a reversal of a 1970s "pact" named for the opposite of this concept.
question.answerHtml: memory [or mémoire; or memoria; accept word forms of remembering; accept lieu de mémoire; accept Historical Memory Law]

swap.text: One of Abd-ar-Rahman's accomplishments was to oust Ordono the Bad from the throne of Leon and reinstall a ruler of this name dubbed the "Fat." Another king with this name ruled Navarre during the early 1000's and occupied both Castile and Leon during his reign.
swap.clue: A "Great" king of Pamplona of this name's posthumous division of his lands led to a war between Jimenez kings of Castile, Navarre, and Aragon, all of this name, that was resolved when Aragon's one got tossed off a cliff.
